entries.title: Psalms 109:1
segments: The full application of this psalm is to Christ.  To David, as the earthly head of God's people, acting in their behalf and persecuted for their sake, it had a real but subordinate application.  The imprecations which it contains were uttered by God's Spirit.

They are the denunciation of God's vengeance upon the persecutors of his people, whose cause David represented in  a lower sense, and which was to be afterwards represented in the fullest sense in the person of the promised Messiah.

entries.title: Psalms 109:4
segments: The unfailing resource of God's people in trouble is prayer.  However they may be treated by men, his ears are ever open to their cry.

entries.title: Psalms 109:5
segments: The Saviour's love was rewarded with hatred and persecution, and his disciples should not be surprised or dismayed if they are called to suffer in like manner.

entries.title: Psalms 109:6
segments: Him; probably referring to Ahithophel, whose treachery foreshadowed that of Judas, to whom the words are applied in the New Testament.
At his right hand; as an enemy and accuser.

The meaning is, that the traitor shall be given over to the power of Satan. The curses enumerated in this and the following verses, are those threatened in the law against the wicked and their posterity. 
 
The hatred and malice which men show towards Christ's faithful servants he will consider as shown towards himself, and will recompense accordingly; and as there is no sin so great as that of persecuting Christ, whether in his own person or that of his followers, so there is no sin which brings upon men such a terrible retribution.

entries.title: Psalms 109:9
segments: The rejection of Christ by one generation has often been a source of dreadful misery to many following generations.  This applies alike to families and nations.

entries.title: Psalms 109:14
segments: The iniquity of his fathers; compare
.  It is by consenting to and imitating the evil deeds of their fathers, that the children bring their iniquities upon themselves.

entries.title: Psalms 109:16
segments: Persecution of the poor and needy is highly displeasing to God, and brings down his curse on those who inflict it.

entries.title: Psalms 109:21
segments: The necessities of sinners furnish an occasion for God's glorifying himself in the display of his mercy and grace; and this may be pleaded as a reason why he should interpose in their behalf.

entries.title: Psalms 109:23
segments:
When it declineth; is stretched out at evening, and ready to vanish. 
 
  As the locust; when driven before the wind.

entries.title: Psalms 109:26
segments: All the hope of the penitent is in the mercy of God through Jesus Christ, and to him they apply for the blessings which they need.

entries.title: Psalms 109:27
segments: That this is thy hand; that this deliverance for which I pray comes from thee.

entries.title: Psalms 109:28
segments: When God blesses us the curses of the wicked can do us no harm.

entries.title: Psalms 109:30
segments: Among the multitude; when I pay my vows for thy deliverance before the great congregation.  See notes on
